stages.name: Severan peace
stages.desc: Quiet provinces under the young emperor Severus Alexander

stages.name: Frontier at war
stages.desc: Rhine and Danube lands where the armies are fighting

stages.name: Loyal to Maximinus
stages.desc: Obeys the soldier-emperor and his tax-collectors

stages.name: Backing the Gordians
stages.desc: Africa's own emperors, proclaimed at Thysdrus

stages.name: Backing the Senate
stages.desc: Rome's Senate and the emperors it chose against Maximinus

stages.name: Divided or uncertain
stages.desc: Allegiance contested or not recorded in our sources

states.name: France
timeline: Gaul: the Three Gauls and Narbonensis, governed from Lugdunum and Narbo
Germanic raids across the upper Rhine; the frontier province reached into today's Alsace
Near Mainz, the Rhine army murders Alexander and proclaims Maximinus
Maximinus leaves the Rhine for the Danube
How Gaul answered the Senate's call against Maximinus is not recorded

states.name: Morocco
timeline: Mauretania Tingitana: olive presses and townhouses at Volubilis
The far western province accepts Maximinus
Tingitana's side in the civil war of 238 is not recorded

states.name: Spain
timeline: Hispania: the oil of Baetica, now rivalled in Rome by African oil
The Spanish provinces accept Maximinus; the future emperor Decius governs Tarraconensis
Spain's stance in 238 is unclear in the sources

states.name: Libya
timeline: Tripolitania, part of Africa Proconsularis: Leptis Magna, hometown of Septimius Severus, rebuilt in marble
The olive towns of Tripolitania accept the new emperor Maximinus
Tripolitania lies in Gordian's own province (Cyrenaica, further east, belonged to Crete)

states.name: Tunisia
timeline: Africa Proconsularis: olive estates around Thysdrus, Hadrumetum and Sufetula ship oil to Rome
Thysdrus, rich on olive oil, builds villas floored with mosaics and a great amphitheatre
The province recognises Maximinus; his procurators press the landowners for money
Young landowners kill the procurator at Thysdrus and proclaim the proconsul Gordian emperor; within weeks Capellianus crushes the revolt

states.name: Hungary
timeline: Pannonia: the legions of Aquincum and Brigetio guard the Danube
Pannonia's legions back their former comrade Maximinus
Maximinus fights the Sarmatians across the Danube
Pannonia's legions march with Maximinus into Italy

states.name: Italy
timeline: Severus Alexander becomes emperor in Rome at thirteen; his mother Julia Mamaea guides him
Alexander leaves Rome for the war against the new Persian empire
Rome accepts Maximinus, an emperor who never sets foot in the city
Confiscations and the seizure of city funds turn the Senate and people against Maximinus
The Senate backs the Gordians, then elects Pupienus and Balbinus; Aquileia holds out against Maximinus

states.name: Serbia
timeline: Sirmium and Moesia Superior: a frontier of forts along the Danube
The Danube legions back Maximinus
Maximinus makes Sirmium his winter headquarters for wars against Dacians and Sarmatians
At Sirmium Maximinus hears of the revolt and marches for Italy

states.name: Croatia
timeline: Dalmatia and southern Pannonia: Salona on the Adriatic, Siscia on the Sava
Illyrian lands, home of many of Maximinus's soldiers, back the new emperor
Maximinus's army marches west along the Sava toward Italy

states.name: Algeria
timeline: Numidia and Mauretania Caesariensis: the Third Augustan Legion guards the frontier from Lambaesis
Numidia's legion and governor accept Maximinus
Capellianus, governor of Numidia, stays loyal to Maximinus and marches on Carthage

events.title: A boy emperor
events.text: After the murder of Elagabalus, his thirteen-year-old cousin Severus Alexander becomes emperor, guided by his mother Julia Mamaea.

events.title: Oil for Rome
events.text: Ships from Africa unload amphorae of olive oil at Ostia, feeding the free oil ration Septimius Severus had given Rome.

events.title: Ulpian murdered
events.text: The jurist Ulpian, Alexander's praetorian prefect, is killed by his own guardsmen.

events.title: Leptis Magna
events.text: The hometown of Septimius Severus glitters with the marble forum and basilica he gave it.

events.title: Baetican oil
events.text: Spain's oil still sails down the Guadalquivir, but African oil is winning Rome's market.

events.title: Carthage
events.text: Rebuilt as a Roman colony, Carthage is the greatest city of the Latin West after Rome.

events.title: Olive steppe
events.text: Around Sufetula and Thysdrus, olive groves spread across once-dry steppe, worked by tenant farmers.

events.title: Mosaics of Thysdrus
events.text: Rich houses in Thysdrus are floored with mosaics of Dionysus, peacocks and wild beasts.

events.title: Dio's consulship
events.text: The historian Cassius Dio shares the consulship with Alexander, then retires, fearing the soldiers.

events.title: Amphitheatre rises
events.text: Thysdrus builds one of the largest amphitheatres in the Roman world, for some thirty-five thousand spectators.

events.title: Volubilis
events.text: At the far western edge of Roman Africa, Volubilis presses olives in dozens of mills.

events.title: War with Persia
events.text: Alexander leaves Rome to fight the new Sasanian empire, which has invaded Roman Mesopotamia.

events.title: Third Augustan Legion
events.text: Africa's only legion holds its great fortress at Lambaesis, in Numidia.

events.title: Triumph in Rome
events.text: Alexander celebrates a triumph for an inconclusive Persian war.

events.title: Rhine crossed
events.text: Germanic warriors raid across the Rhine; Alexander hurries west to Mainz.

events.title: Alexander killed
events.text: Near Mainz, soldiers angry at his offer to buy peace kill Alexander and his mother.

events.title: Maximinus proclaimed
events.text: The troops acclaim Maximinus, a towering Thracian who rose from the ranks.

events.title: Bishops exiled
events.text: Pontian, bishop of Rome, and the writer Hippolytus are deported to the mines of Sardinia.

events.title: Victory paintings
events.text: Maximinus has huge paintings of his German battles set up before the Senate house.

events.title: Sirmium
events.text: Maximinus winters at Sirmium, his base for wars on the Danube.

events.title: Danube wars
events.text: Campaigns against Sarmatians and Dacians win him new victory titles.

events.title: Decius in Spain
events.text: The senator Decius, a future emperor, governs Hispania Tarraconensis.

events.title: The squeeze
events.text: To pay the army, Maximinus's agents seize private fortunes, city funds and temple treasures.

events.title: Procurator killed
events.text: Young landowners fined by the procurator arm their farm workers and kill him at Thysdrus.

events.title: Gordian proclaimed
events.text: The rebels wrap the nearly eighty-year-old proconsul Gordian in purple and hail him emperor.

events.title: Gordians in Carthage
events.text: Gordian and his son, Gordian the Second, rule from Carthage as joint emperors.

events.title: Senate backs Africa
events.text: The Senate recognises the Gordians and declares Maximinus a public enemy.

events.title: Prefect slain
events.text: Gordian's agents kill Maximinus's praetorian prefect Vitalianus in Rome.

events.title: Capellianus marches
events.text: The loyal governor of Numidia leads his legion and Moorish horsemen on Carthage.

events.title: Battle of Carthage
events.text: Gordian the Second's untrained militia is routed and he is killed.

events.title: Gordian hangs himself
events.text: Hearing of his son's death, the old emperor hangs himself after a reign of about three weeks.

events.title: Reprisals in Africa
events.text: Capellianus's soldiers kill leading citizens and plunder the towns that backed the Gordians.

events.title: Two Senate emperors
events.text: The Senate elects two of its own, Pupienus and Balbinus, to fight Maximinus.

events.title: Gordian the Third
events.text: Rioting crowds force the Senate to name Gordian's thirteen-year-old grandson Caesar.

events.title: March on Italy
events.text: Maximinus's army moves west from the Danube along the Sava toward the Alps.

events.title: Emona abandoned
events.text: The invaders find the first Italian town emptied of people and food.

events.title: Siege of Aquileia
events.text: Led by two senators, Aquileia shuts its gates and holds out against Maximinus.

events.title: Pupienus at Ravenna
events.text: Pupienus gathers troops at Ravenna to defend Italy.

events.title: Maximinus murdered
events.text: Starving and stalled, soldiers of the Second Parthian Legion kill Maximinus and his son in their tent.

events.title: Praetorians strike
events.text: In summer the praetorian guard murders Pupienus and Balbinus; Gordian the Third reigns alone.

events.title: Legion disbanded
events.text: Gordian the Third dissolves the Third Augustan Legion for crushing his family.

chartNote: Share of the area of ten present-day countries, standing in for the Roman provinces on their soil, by each region's allegiance. A simplification: modern borders cut across the provinces, the map moves year by year, so 238 shows the side each region took in that year's civil war, and much of what we know comes from one contemporary historian, Herodian. The vast Saharan parts of Algeria and Libya swing the shares.
